chief_complaint: Management of hypertension and associated cardiometabolic risk factors
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 48-year-old woman with a documented history of essential hypertension (onset 2016), obesity (BMI ≥30, onset 2016), and prediabetes (onset 1998). She reports chronic stress since 2017 and works full‑time. Blood pressure remains in the stage 1 range (137/84 mmHg) despite lisinopril 10 mg daily, and her resting heart rate is elevated at 97 bpm. Laboratory data are limited; the most recent A1c is 5.9 % (prediabetic). No lipid panel or renal function results are available. The last recorded encounter was a burn injury in March 2018. Current medications include lisinopril and a vitamin B12 injection of unclear indication. Overall, her clinical picture reflects persistent cardiometabolic risk with insufficient monitoring and therapeutic optimization.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include a partial thickness burn (2018), burn injury (2018), fractured dental filling (2017), acute bronchitis (2017), gingivitis (2017), a medication review (2017), and a prior status of not being in the labor force (2017). The patient also has a remote history of tubal ligation (2005).

social_determinants: Full‑time employment, chronic stress, criminal record, involvement in risk activities, high‑school education level; no documented smoking or alcohol use.
risk_factor_summary: Blood pressure 137/84 mmHg (stage 1 hypertension), heart rate 97 bpm, A1c 5.9 % (prediabetic), obesity documented but exact BMI missing, no lipid panel or eGFR available. Charlson comorbidity index is 0; clinical complexity rated moderate. Elevated risk involves cardiovascular (hypertension, obesity, prediabetes), metabolic (impaired glucose tolerance), potential renal (hypertension, obesity) and hematologic/neurologic systems (possible B12 deficiency). Psychosocial stressors further increase cardiovascular risk.

clinical_impression: Middle‑aged woman with persistent stage 1 hypertension, obesity, and prediabetes, compounded by chronic stress and limited laboratory monitoring. Cardiovascular and metabolic risk are moderate to high, while data gaps (lipids, renal function, BMI) hinder full risk stratification. Current therapy (lisinopril) may be insufficient; lifestyle interventions and additional work‑up are warranted.
